subject.title: Create example OpenClaw plugin using before_install

question: Should ClawScan own and ship an OpenClaw `before_install` example plugin, or should this integration be maintained and distributed externally?
rationale: The code is feasible, but repository placement, release ownership, hook compatibility, and fail-open versus fail-closed behavior are product and security-policy choices that automation cannot safely select.

options.title: Ship an isolated example
options.body: Add a separately packaged example under a non-CLI integration surface, with explicit security semantics and end-to-end local proof.

options.title: Publish externally
options.body: Maintain the integration as a standalone OpenClaw or ClawHub plugin and link to it from ClawScan integration documentation.

options.title: Remain CLI-only
options.body: Keep ClawScan focused on its CLI and scanner APIs and decline a repository-owned plugin example.

recommendation.title: Ship an isolated example
recommendation.body: Add a separately packaged example under a non-CLI integration surface, with explicit security semantics and end-to-end local proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They proposed the integration, identified the working branch, and have recent merged ownership of the scanner behavior the plugin would invoke.
